data.statement: Restore bounded checkpoint and progress throttling in deterministic chunking while preserving resume-consistent checkpoints and mandatory terminal persistence

acceptance: Under a fixed monotonic clock, deterministic chunking of 1000 narratable paragraphs performs one initial running write, only interval checkpoints at the 200-paragraph policy, and exactly one completed terminal-document write; write count is bounded by ceil(1000/200) plus a small constant rather than approximately 1000.

The 2.0-second checkpoint branch can persist before 200 additional paragraphs, and every persisted running checkpoint has chunks and next_paragraph describing the same processed prefix, including prefixes containing non-narratable separator records.
Cancellation and unexpected failure each persist one terminal cancelled or failed document containing the current consistent chunks/next_paragraph pair before propagating the exception.
Successful completion persists exactly one completed terminal document with next_paragraph set to null and final warnings populated, then returns the report.
Non-terminal progress callbacks are limited by the 0.1-second policy while the terminal completed progress update is always emitted.
Existing deterministic resume, cancellation, separator-prefix, source-fingerprint mismatch, and single-document contract tests remain green.
The AI-assisted chunking implementation and its one-write-per-model-window behavior are unchanged.
The complete pytest and Ruff repository gates pass, with traceability and coverage audits free of blocking findings.
data.reason: The defect is localized to one deterministic loop, the intended policies already exist as unused helpers/constants, the persisted schema is unchanged, and focused resume/cancellation contracts bound the risk.
scope: In scope: deterministic chunk_text checkpoint/progress scheduling, focused write-count/progress/resume regression coverage, the existing recoverable-checkpoint requirement, one bounded-performance requirement, the Cleanup/Chunking V2 specification, and Text Chunking component documentation. Out of scope: AI-assisted chunking, checkpoint interval values, chunk semantics, persistence-service atomic-write mechanics, document schema changes, legacy state-layer cleanup tracked by issue #36, and unrelated performance work.
data.source: Gitea issue #31: http://192.168.1.15:3001/dpasare/2026_AudioMancer/issues/31; remediation order in issue #40
data.understanding: Deterministic chunking currently rewrites and revalidates the growing chunks_text.json document and emits progress after every processed paragraph. Restore the existing 200-paragraph or 2.0-second checkpoint policy and 0.1-second non-terminal progress policy inside chunk_text, while preserving a consistent chunks/next_paragraph resume boundary and mandatory completed, cancelled, and failed terminal persistence. The AI-assisted chunking path and canonical document schema remain unchanged.

data.rationale: Bounded checkpoint cadence prevents quadratic full-document validation, serialization, and fsync work while retaining time-bounded recovery.
data.requirement: Deterministic chunking shall persist non-terminal checkpoints after at most 200 additional processed paragraphs or 2.0 elapsed monotonic seconds.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest: deterministic chunking file passed 14 tests; 1000-paragraph fixed-clock writes are bounded and the 2.0-second branch persists a consistent separator prefix.

data.rationale: Progress callbacks must remain responsive without imposing per-paragraph UI and cross-thread overhead on large documents.
data.requirement: Deterministic chunking shall emit non-terminal progress no more often than once per 0.1 elapsed monotonic seconds.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest: deterministic chunking file passed 14 tests; controlled-clock progress emits no more often than 0.1 seconds and always emits completion.

data.rationale: Successful publication must expose one unambiguous final document without duplicate terminal writes.
data.requirement: Deterministic chunking shall persist exactly one completed terminal document before returning a successful report.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest: captured persistence sequence contains exactly one completed terminal document with next_paragraph null after bounded running checkpoints.

data.rationale: Operator cancellation must retain the current resumable prefix without swallowing the cancellation signal.
data.requirement: Deterministic chunking shall persist one cancelled terminal document before propagating cancellation.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest: deterministic and single-document contract files passed; cancellation persists one resumable terminal document before OperationCancelledError propagates.

data.rationale: Unexpected failures must leave an inspectable resumable boundary while preserving the original exception.
data.requirement: Deterministic chunking shall persist one failed terminal document before propagating an unexpected processing exception.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest: an injected processing exception persists one resume-consistent failed terminal document and re-raises the original exception.

data.rationale: Resume validation must observe one self-consistent boundary even when processed paragraphs do not produce narratable chunks.
data.requirement: Every persisted deterministic chunking checkpoint shall encode the exact processed paragraph prefix in its chunks and next_paragraph values.
